sections.markdown:
## C — Sharing the road: commercial vehicle no-zones, motorcycles and mopeds, stopping for school buses, bicycles, riding in a truck bed, pedestrians and crosswalks, and blind or visually impaired pedestrians
Knowledge domain: how to drive safely around large trucks and buses and their blind spots, what makes motorcycles and mopeds different, when Nevada requires you to stop for a school bus, how to share lanes with cyclists, who may ride in a truck bed, and what drivers owe pedestrians, including people who are blind or visually impaired.

FACT_ID: sec09-F01 | anchor: A01
Large commercial vehicles cannot maneuver like cars, have much bigger blind spots, and need more time and space to slow down or stop. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec09-F02 | anchor: A01
Most crashes between large trucks and smaller cars are caused by the car drivers, and the people in the cars are far more likely to be killed or hurt. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec09-F03 | anchor: A01
The no-zone is the set of blind spots around a large truck or bus, at its sides, rear and front, where a car effectively disappears from the driver's view. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec09-F04 | anchor: A01
The right-side no-zone is doubly dangerous because trucks and buses swing wide when turning right. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec09-F05 | anchor: A01
Do not linger beside a truck or bus: if you cannot see the driver's face in their side mirror, the driver cannot see you. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec09-F06 | anchor: A02
Large trucks and buses need nearly twice the time and distance cars need to stop, so cutting in front and slowing can get you rear-ended. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-F07 | anchor: A02
After passing a truck or bus, wait until its whole front shows in your rearview mirror before moving into its lane, and then do not slow down. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-F08 | anchor: A02
Do not tailgate a truck or bus: its driver cannot see you directly behind, you cannot see the road beyond it, and a sudden stop leaves you nowhere to go. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-F09 | anchor: A02
Never pass behind a commercial truck that is backing up, because its driver cannot see vehicles or people directly behind it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-F10 | anchor: A02
Trucks and buses may swing wide left to make a right turn, or wide right to make a left turn, so never try to squeeze between one and the curb. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-F11 | anchor: A02
Motorcyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as other drivers, including the right to use a full traffic lane. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-F12 | anchor: A02
With the drivers' consent, motorcycles and mopeds may ride at most two abreast in a single lane; without consent they must ride staggered (NRS 486.351). [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-F13 | anchor: A02
Motorcycles are small, so they are harder to see, may seem farther away than they really are, and their speed is hard to judge. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-F14 | anchor: A02
Most motorcycle turn signals do not cancel themselves, so before a turn or lane change that depends on a rider's path, be sure what the rider is actually doing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-F15 | anchor: A02
Approaching a motorcycle from behind, begin slowing earlier than you would for a car and keep a generous gap. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-F16 | anchor: A03
Always dim your headlights when approaching a motorcycle, because riders steer by balance and high-beam glare is more dangerous to them than to car or truck drivers. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec09-F17 | anchor: A03
Leave even more following distance behind a motorcycle when it is raining or the road is slippery. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec09-F18 | anchor: A03
Riding a motorcycle requires a special endorsement on a Nevada driver's license. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec09-F19 | anchor: A03
Nevada sets a moped apart by motor size, a maximum of two brake horsepower, and a top speed of 30 mph on flat or nearly flat ground. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec09-F20 | anchor: A03
Moped riders must stay in the far right lane unless there is only one lane, they are preparing a left turn within a quarter mile, the right lane is unsafe, or a police officer directs otherwise. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec09-F21 | anchor: A03
Mopeds must be registered with the DMV for a one-time fee but need no insurance, and moped riders and passengers must wear helmets in Nevada. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec09-F22 | anchor: A03
You must stop at any location for a school bus showing a flashing red signal, and you may not pass it until the bus driver turns those lights off (NRS 484B.353). [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec09-F23 | anchor: A03
On a divided highway, you have to stop for a school bus only when you are traveling in the same direction as the bus. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec09-F24 | anchor: A04
A motorist who causes even a minor collision with a bicycle, or deliberately interferes with a cyclist, may be charged with reckless driving, which can bring a license suspension. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec09-F25 | anchor: A04
Cyclists may ride in a traffic lane, keeping as far right as practicable unless they are preparing to turn or passing another vehicle. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec09-F26 | anchor: A04
At intersections, motorists must yield to cyclists just as they would to other vehicles and pedestrians. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec09-F27 | anchor: A04
Motorists may not stop, park or drive in a bike lane or bike path except to enter or leave an alley or driveway, on official duty, when police direct it, or in an emergency. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec09-F28 | anchor: A04
Never speed up to pass a cyclist just before you turn, and check for cyclists before opening a parked car's door or backing out of a driveway or lot. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec09-F29 | anchor: A05
In Nevada, no one under 18 may ride in a pickup bed or on a flatbed truck on a paved highway, except in a parade authorized by a local authority or while farming or ranching. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec09-F30 | anchor: A05
Drivers must use due care to avoid hitting a pedestrian, and a driver who causes any pedestrian collision, however minor, can face a reckless driving charge. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec09-F31 | anchor: A05
It is illegal to overtake a vehicle that is slowing or stopped until you have slowed enough to see why it slowed or stopped. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec09-F32 | anchor: A05
A crosswalk exists wherever two streets meet, including a T intersection, whether or not it is painted. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec09-F33 | anchor: A05
When your light turns green, yield to anyone still crossing, and pedestrians have the right-of-way over drivers turning right. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec09-F34 | anchor: A05
Yield, slow or stop for a pedestrian in a crosswalk on your half of the road or the half you are turning into, or one coming so close from the other half as to be in danger. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec09-F35 | anchor: A06
When stopping for a blind or visually impaired pedestrian, stop no more than five feet from the crosswalk, since such a pedestrian uses your engine sound as a guide. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec09-F36 | anchor: A06
Give a blind or visually impaired pedestrian time to decide, about 3 to 4 seconds; if the person steps back and pulls in the cane, you may go. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0067]

Misconceptions: most car-truck crashes are not the truck driver's fault, car drivers cause most of them; seeing the truck in your mirror is not enough, you must see the driver's face in their mirror to be seen; a crosswalk does not need paint to exist; on a divided highway, oncoming traffic does not stop for a school bus; motorcycles may share a lane two abreast only with consent; mopeds need registration but not insurance.
Mnemonics: no face, no space beside a truck; whole front in the mirror before you merge back; red lights on the bus, everybody stops, except across a divided highway; two abreast with consent; quarter mile for the moped left turn.
Glossary: no-zone means the blind-spot area around a large truck or bus; squeeze play means a car slipping between a wide-turning truck and the curb; endorsement means an extra privilege added to a license, such as for motorcycles; moped means a small motor vehicle limited in horsepower and top speed; unmarked crosswalk means the legal crossing at any intersection even without paint.
Dynamic facts: moped registration fees and engine-size details are on the DMV website, and the yearly car-and-truck crash figure carries no source year, so both should be refreshed from current official sources.
